Rashi on Arakhin 20b:10:1.hebrew: ואיכא דמתני לה - להא סוגיא דרב יהודה ואביי ורמי בר חמא:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:10:1.english: And there are those who teach it - [this discussion] of Rav Yehudah, Abaye, and Rami bar Chama:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:10:2.hebrew: אע"פ שחלטו כהן - שאמר: טמא הוא ועומד לנתץ. כל זמן שלא נתצו, אומר לו משכיר לשוכר: הרי שלך לפניך, ולא אשכיר לך בית אחר, שהרי בית שהשכרתי לך קיים:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:10:2.english: Even though a priest confirmed it [as impure] - [meaning] that he said: It is impure and is destined to be dismantled. As long as it has not [yet] been dismantled, the lessor says to the renter: "That which is yours is before you, and I will not rent you another house, for the house that I rented to you still stands."

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:10:3.hebrew: נתצו - כהן, חייב משכיר להעמיד בית אחר לשוכר, דמשום מזליה דמשכיר הוא, שנחשד על הגזל או על צרות העין:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:10:3.english: [If] he dismantled it - [i.e., if] the priest [dismantled it], the lessor is obligated to provide another house for the lessee, because it is on account of the lessor's [bad] fortune [that the house was afflicted], since he is suspected of robbery or of stinginess:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:1:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא - אע"ג דעמד בדין הנודר קודם מותו, הואיל ולא אמדו את הנידר בחיי הנודר, לא אשתעבדו נכסי דיתמי:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:1:1.english: Lest you say - Although the one who vowed stood in judgment before his death, since [the court] did not assess the object of the vow during the lifetime of the one who vowed, the property of the orphans [i.e., the heirs] is not liened [to the debt]:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:1:2.hebrew: גלויי מלתא בעלמא הוא - לגלות מהו הסכום שחייב, והואיל ונידר קיים, אמדינן ליה:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:1:2.english: It is a mere disclosure of the matter - [The assessment serves] to reveal how much he is obligated [to pay]. And since the object of the vow still exists, we assess it:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:2:1.english: And this house is an offering - [consecrated] for the maintenance of the Temple:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:2:2.hebrew: ונפל הבית - קודם שהחזיק בו גזבר:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:2:2.english: And the house collapsed - before the treasurer took possession of it:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:3:1.hebrew: לא שנו - שבמשנה דכי אמר "עלי" חייב לשלם, אלא דאמר "דמי שור זה עלי", דאם אבד השור, הדמים לא אבדו, דהא לא אמר "דמים הללו", ולא היו בעין:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:3:1.english: They taught only - [in the mishna] that when one says "[it is incumbent] upon me," he is obligated to pay, only when he said, "the value [of this bull] is incumbent upon me." For if the bull is lost, the money is not lost, since he did not say "this money," and [the coins] were not [yet] in existence [as designated funds]:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:3:2.english: It is incumbent upon me to bring it - to take the trouble [of bringing it] until it is offered:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:5:1.hebrew: ה"נ דקאמר דמי - וכדאוקימנא לקמן, דאמר: יקדש שור זה לדמיו, והדמים עלי עולה. הלכך השור קדוש, דהאמר "יקדש השור"; ואם מת, חייב באחריותו, דהאמר "עלי". והכא ליכא למימר כדאמר לעיל, דהתם כיון דאמר "זה", למפטר נפשיה מאחריות אתי, ו"עלי" אטורח הבאה קאי. אבל הכא דלא הוו דמים קמיה, ולא אמר "הללו", ודאי "עלי" אאחריות קאי. והאי דקאמר "זה", הכי קאמר: שור זה יהא קדוש עד שאמכרנו ואביא דמיו:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:5:1.english: Here too, where he said "the value of" - And as we established below, that he said: "This bull shall be sanctified for its value, and the money [value] is incumbent upon me as a burnt offering." Therefore the bull is sanctified, because he said, "the bull shall be sanctified"; and if it dies, he is liable for its responsibility, because he said "[it is incumbent] upon me." But here one cannot say as [was] said above, for there, since he said "this," he comes to free himself from responsibility, and "upon me" refers to the burden of bringing [it]. But here, where the money was not before him, and he did not say "these," certainly "upon me" refers to responsibility. And as for his saying "this," he means as follows: This bull shall be sanctified until I sell it and bring its value:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:6:1.hebrew: השור חולין - דלא הקדיש אלא מעות, והם דמי השור לכשימכר:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:6:1.english: The bull is non-sacred - for he consecrated only money, [namely] the monetary value of the bull when it will be sold:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:6:2.hebrew: אינו חייב באחריותו - שהרי לא נמכר, ונמצא שלא הקדיש כלום:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:6:2.english: He does not bear responsibility for it - since it was not sold, and it turns out that he did not consecrate anything:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:6:3.hebrew: אבל חייב באחריות דמיו - אם נמכר השור, וקדשו הדמים, ואבדו, חייב באחריותו:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:6:3.english: But he does bear responsibility for its monetary value - If the bull was sold and the money became consecrated, and [the money] was lost, he is liable for its replacement:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:7:1.hebrew: רישא דאמר יקדש השור לדמיו - והלכך חייב באחריותו, שהרי חל קדושת דמים על השור, והוא קיבל עליו אחריות דמיו. והאי "עלי אחריות" הוי, הואיל ואדמים קאי, ודמים לא הוו קמיה דלימא "הללו":
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:7:1.english: The first clause, where he said: Let the bull be consecrated for its monetary value - And therefore he is liable for its responsibility, since the sanctity of monetary value has taken effect on the bull, and he has taken upon himself responsibility for its value. And this is [considered as saying] "upon me is responsibility," since he is standing [in his vow] on the monetary value, and there is no money before him such that he could say "these":

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:7:2.hebrew: סיפא דאמר לכשיבואו דמיו יקדשו - הלכך אינו חייב באחריותו, דכיון דמת השור ולא בא לכלל דמים, נמצא שלא הקדיש כלום:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:7:2.english: The latter clause, where he said: "When its monetary value comes, it shall be consecrated" - Therefore he is not liable for its responsibility, for since the bull died and did not come to [the point of being sold for] money, it turns out that he did not consecrate anything:

Rashi on Arakhin 20b:8:1.hebrew: ר"מ היא - דתניא: הרי את מקודשת לי לאחר שאתגייר, או לאחר שתתגיירי, כו' ר"מ אומר: מקודשת:
Rashi on Arakhin 20b:8:1.english: It is [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir - For it was taught [in a baraita]: [If a man says to a woman,] "You are betrothed to me after I convert," [or] "after you convert," etc., Rabbi Meir says: She is betrothed:

Tosafot on Arakhin 20b:10:1.hebrew: אע"פ שחלטו כהן אומר לו הרי שלך לפניך - אור"י דמהכא משמע דבית מנוגע המוחלט מותר בהנאה, ומש"ה אומר לו "הרי שלך לפניך", דדמי להא דתנן פרק האומנין (ב"מ עח. ושם): שכר חמור והבריקה או שנעשית אנגריא, אומר לו "הרי שלך לפניך"; דאי אמרינן דבית הנחלט אסור בהנאה, אם כן הוי כי "מתה או נשברה", דתנן התם: חייב להעמיד לו חמור אחר. וקשה למורי מהא דאמר בתורת כהנים גבי בגדים: "צרעת ממארת" — תן לה מארה, שלא יהנה ממנו; משמע דאסור בהנאה. וכן משמע בפרק מצות חליצה (יבמות קג:): א"ר פפא משמיה דרבא, [סנדל] המוסגר לא תחלוץ, ואם חלצה חליצתה כשרה; סנדל המוחלט לא תחלוץ, ואם חלצה חליצתה פסולה. ופרש"י שם, דסנדל המוסגר לא תחלוץ בו לכתחלה משום גזירה דסנדל המוחלט, מיהו אם חלצה חליצתה כשרה, משום דמצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו; אלמא משמע סנדל המוחלט אסור בהנאה! וצ"ל דאין הכי נמי דהוא אסור בהנאה, והא דאמר הכא דאומר לו "הרי שלך לפניך", היינו כגון דא"ל "בית זה", וכיון דהוא בעין, אינו חייב להעמיד לו בית אחר, מיהו הוא הפסיד שכרו, והוי כמו "מתה או נשברה", דאמר התם: חייב להעמיד לו חמור אחר, ופרש"י שם: או יפסיד שכרו:
Tosafot on Arakhin 20b:10:1.english: Even though a priest confirmed it, he says to him, "That which is yours is before you" - Rabbeinu Yitzḥak says that from here it is implied that a leprous house that has been confirmed [as impure] is permitted for benefit, and for that reason he says to him, "That which is yours is before you," for it is similar to that which we learned in the chapter [entitled] HaOmanin (Bava Metzia 78a and elsewhere): [If] one rented a donkey and it went blind or was conscripted into royal service, he says to him, "That which is yours is before you." For if we were to say that a confirmed [leprous] house is forbidden for benefit, if so, it would be like [the case of] "it died or broke [a limb]," regarding which we learned there: he is obligated to provide another donkey for him. And it is difficult for my teacher from that which is stated in Torat Kohanim regarding garments: "a malignant leprosy" — put a curse upon it, that one may not derive benefit from it; [this] implies that it is forbidden for benefit. And so too is it implied in the chapter [entitled] Mitzvat Ḥalitza (Yevamot 103b): Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava: [With] a [sandal] that is quarantined [for leprosy], she should not perform ḥalitza, but if she performed ḥalitza, her ḥalitza is valid; [with] a sandal that is confirmed [as leprous], she should not perform ḥalitza, and if she performed ḥalitza, her ḥalitza is invalid. And Rashi explained there that with a quarantined sandal she should not perform ḥalitza ab initio because of a decree on account of a confirmed sandal; however, if she performed ḥalitza, her ḥalitza is valid, because mitzvot were not given for [the sake of] deriving benefit. Thus, it implies [that] a confirmed sandal is forbidden for benefit! And one must say that indeed it is forbidden for benefit, and that which [the baraita] says here that he says to him, "That which is yours is before you," refers to a case where he said to him, "this house"; and since it is [still] intact, he is not obligated to provide another house for him, however, he loses his rent, and it is like [the case of] "it died or broke [a limb]," where it states there: he is obligated to provide another donkey for him, and Rashi explained there: or he loses his rent:

Tosafot on Arakhin 20b:3:1.hebrew: אמר ר' חייא בר רב ל"ש אלא דאמר דמי שור זה עלי עולה אבל אמר שור זה עלי עולה כיון דאמר זה ומת אינו חייב באחריותו עלי להביאו קאמר - כלומר, לטרוח עד שיתקרב. וא"ת: א"כ רישא דמתני' דקתני "שור זה עולה, מת השור פטור מלשלם", למה [לאשמועינן] אפילו אמר "עלי" (נראה כן) הדין [כן] דפטור מלשלם, כדמסיק ר' חייא בר רב? ואור"י דכולה מתני', בין רישא בין סיפא, מיירי דאמר "דמי". וה"פ דמתני': "דמי שור זה עולה, דמי בית זה קרבן, מת השור, נפל הבית — פטור מלשלם", כיון דלא אמר "עלי"; אבל אמר "דמי שור זה עלי עולה, דמי בית זה עלי קרבן, מת השור ונפל הבית — חייב לשלם". והכי איתא בפ"ק דר"ה (דף ו. ושם): איזהו נדר ואיזהו נדבה? נדר דאמר "עלי", נדבה דאמר "הרי זו". מה בין נדר לנדבה? נדר, מת או נגנב — חייב באחריותו; נדבה, מת או נגנב — אינו חייב באחריותו. והא דתניא במתני' "שור זה", נראה דרבותא אשמועינן, דאע"ג דאמר "זה", כיון דאמר "עלי" חייב באחריותו. ואר"י דלכאורה משמע דכי אמר "דמי שור זה עלי עולה", גוף השור הוא חולין ואין בו קדושה, דדמי לאומר "דמי שור של פלוני עלי", דגוף השור הוא חולין, דאין אדם מקדיש שור חבירו. ולא דמי למקדיש זכר לדמיו, דאמר בתמורה (דף יט: ושם) דקדוש קדושת הגוף, דמגו דנחתא ביה קדושת דמים נחתא ביה קדושת הגוף; דהתם מיירי כדאמר "יקדש שור זה לדמיו". וה"נ איתא בסמוך בשמעתין, דכי אמר "יקדש השור לדמיו" דגוף השור קדוש:
Tosafot on Arakhin 20b:3:1.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav said: They taught [in the mishna] only where he said "the value of this ox is incumbent upon me as a burnt offering," but if he said "this ox is incumbent upon me as a burnt offering," since he said "this" and it died, he is not liable for its responsibility; "incumbent upon me" he meant to bring it - That is, to exert himself until it is offered. And if you ask: If so, [why does] the first clause of the mishna, which teaches "[If one said:] This ox is a burnt offering, [and] the ox died, he is exempt from paying," [need to] teach us [this]? Even if he said "incumbent upon me," (it seems so) the law [is thus], that he is exempt from paying, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav concludes? And Rabbi Yitzḥak says that the entire mishna, both the first clause and the latter clause, speaks of one who said "the value." And this is the meaning of the mishna: "[If one said:] The value of this ox is a burnt offering, [or] the value of this house is a sacrifice, [and] the ox died [or] the house collapsed — he is exempt from paying," since he did not say "incumbent upon me"; but if he said "the value of this ox is incumbent upon me as a burnt offering, the value of this house is incumbent upon me as a sacrifice," [and] the ox died or the house collapsed — he is liable to pay. And so it is stated in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (6a): What is a vow and what is a freewill offering? A vow is where he said "incumbent upon me"; a freewill offering is where he said "behold this." What is the difference between a vow and a freewill offering? A vow — if it died or was stolen, he is liable for its responsibility; a freewill offering — if it died or was stolen, he is not liable for its responsibility. And as for that which the mishna teaches "this ox," it seems that [the mishna] teaches us a novelty: that although he said "this," since he said "incumbent upon me," he is liable for its responsibility. And Rabbi Yitzḥak says that at first glance it seems that when he says "the value of this ox is incumbent upon me as a burnt offering," the body of the ox is non-sacred and has no sanctity, similar to one who says "the value of so-and-so's ox is incumbent upon me," where the body of the ox is non-sacred, since a person cannot consecrate his fellow's ox. And it is not like one who consecrates a male animal for its value, of which it says in Temurah (19b) that it has the sanctity of the body, for since the sanctity of value took effect upon it, the sanctity of the body took effect upon it; for there it speaks of one who said "let this ox be consecrated for its value." And so too it is stated shortly in our passage, that when he says "let the ox be consecrated for its value," the body of the ox is sacred:

Tosafot on Arakhin 20b:4:1.hebrew: מיתיבי שור זה עולה כו' שור זה עלי עולה השור הקדש ומועלין בו מת או נגנב (אינו) חייב באחריותו - אלמא לא אמרינן "עלי להביאו קאמר", וקשיא לר' חייא. ומשני: מי אלימא ממתניתין דאוקימנא דקאמר דמי? הכא נמי דקאמר דמי. וקשה, לפי מה דפי' דגופו חולין, ובהא ברייתא קתני דשור קדוש. ולפי מה דפירש"י הכא ניחא, וזה לשונו: הכא נמי דקאמר דמי, וכדאוקימנא לקמן דקאמר "יקדש השור לדמיו והדמים עלי עולה", הלכך השור קדוש, דהא אמר "יקדש השור"; ואם מת חייב באחריותו, דהא "עלי" אמר. והכא לא אמר "עלי להביאם קאמר", דכיון דלא הוו דמים קמיה ולא אמר "דמים הללו עלי עולה", ליכא למימר כדאמר לעיל, דהתם כיון דאמר "זה", למפטר נפשיה מאחריות קאתי, ו"עלי" אטורח הבאה קאי; אבל הכא דלא הוו הדמים קמיה ולא אמר "הללו", ודאי "עלי" אאחריות קאי. והא דקאמר "זה", ה"ק: שור זה יהיה הקדש עד שאמכרנו ואביא דמיו. עכ"ל רש"י:
Tosafot on Arakhin 20b:4:1.english: They raised an objection: "This bull is a burnt offering, etc." [and] "This bull is incumbent upon me as a burnt offering, the bull is consecrated and one is liable for misuse of it; if it died or was stolen, he is liable for its responsibility" - Evidently we do not say that "incumbent upon me" means [that he undertook] to bring it; and this is difficult for Rabbi Ḥiyya. And [the Gemara] answers: Is this stronger than the Mishnah, which we established as [a case where] he said "its value"? Here too, he said "its value." But this is difficult, according to what [Tosafot] explained that its body is non-sacred, whereas in this baraita it teaches that the bull is sacred. And according to what Rashi explained, it works out well here, and these are his words: Here too, he said "its value," as we established below, where he said, "Let the bull be sanctified for its value, and the value is incumbent upon me as a burnt offering." Therefore the bull is sacred, since he said, "Let the bull be sanctified"; and if it died he is liable for its responsibility, since he said "incumbent upon me." And here, [the baraita does] not [mean that] he said "incumbent upon me" [meaning] to bring them, because since the money was not before him and he did not say, "This money is incumbent upon me as a burnt offering," one cannot say as [the Gemara] said above — for there, since he said "this," he came to exempt himself from responsibility, and "incumbent upon me" refers to the burden of bringing; but here, where the money was not before him and he did not say "this," certainly "incumbent upon me" refers to responsibility. And as for that which [the baraita] says "this," it means as follows: This bull shall be consecrated until I sell it and bring its value. End of Rashi's words:

Tosafot on Arakhin 20b:6:1.hebrew: והא מדסיפא דקאמר דמי רישא דלא קאמר דמי דקתני סיפא כו' - וה"ה דהוה מצי למיפרך בהדיא מסיפא אמתני', לפי מה דפי' ר' חייא בר רב, דקתני בסיפא: "דמי זה עלי עולה — השור חולין ואין מועלין בו, מת או נגנב אינו חייב באחריותו", ובמתני' תנן דחייב לשלם; אלא לפי מה שהתחיל לאקשויי מרישא, סיים קושייתו עלה. ולפי התירוץ ניחא הכל. [אבל] קשיא על הא דאיתא בפ' בתרא דחולין (דף קלט. ושם): המקדיש מנה לבדק הבית ונגנב או שאבד — רבי יוחנן אמר: חייב באחריותו עד שיבא ליד הגזבר, ורשב"ל אמר: כל היכא דאיתיה בי גזא דרחמנא איתיה, דכתיב: "לה' הארץ ומלואה". וקדשי בדק הבית אע"ג דאמר "עלי" לא מחייב? והא תנן: "האומר שור זה עולה, בית זה קרבן — מת השור ונפל הבית פטור לשלם; שור זה עלי עולה, בית זה עלי קרבן — מת השור ונפל הבית חייב לשלם"! ומאי קפריך? הא דרשב"ל מיירי כשהפריש המנה שהקדיש, ומש"ה קאמר דכל היכא דאיתיה בי גזא דרחמנא איתיה ואינו חייב לשלם; וההיא דמתני' בשלא הפריש כלום, ומש"ה קתני דחייב לשלם, דהא אוקימנא דהשור גופיה חולין! ונראה דלית ליה להאי סוגיא דהתם הא דר' חייא בר רב דמוקי למתני' בדמי. לכך נראה לר"י דהכא במתני' דגוף השור קדוש, כמו מקדיש זכר לדמיו, דקדוש קדושת הגוף; ולא דמי לאומר "שור חבירו עליו" דאין גופו קדוש, דהתם אין אדם יכול להקדיש ממון חבירו, ומיהו כל מה דמצי למתפיס ביה הוא מתפיס, אבל הכא שהשור שלו, כי אמר "דמי שור זה עלי עולה", גוף השור קדוש. והשתא ניחא דפריך בפרק בתרא דחולין (ג"ז שם) מהאי מתני' ארשב"ל, דכיון דגוף השור קדוש, הוי כמו הפרישו, ודמי למקדיש מנה לבדק הבית. וניחא נמי בשמעתין, דפריך מברייתא ד"שור זה עלי עולה וכו'", ומשני דקאמר דמי, והשור הוי הקדש כדקתני, וה"נ מתני' הוי גוף השור הקדש. ומיהו תימה קצת: אמאי צריך לאוקמי כדמסיק רישא, דאמר "יקדש שור לדמיו"? בלא"ה נמי, כיון דאמר "דמי שור זה עלי עולה", הוי גוף השור הקדש! וצ"ל דה"פ: רישא כי הוה אמר "יקדש שור לדמיו", והוי שור הקדש. ועי"ל דהא דאר"ח בר רב "לא שנו אלא דאמר דמי שור זה עלי עולה", פי': דאמר "יקדש שור לדמיו ודמיו עולה", והוי גוף השור קדוש. ובהכי ניחא כולה שמעתא, וניחא נמי האי דפ"ב דחולין (ג"ז שם), ופריך ממתני' דהכא אר' שמעון בן לקיש, דכיון דגוף השור קדוש, הוי כאילו הפריש, ודמי למקדיש מנה לבדק הבית:
Tosafot on Arakhin 20b:6:1.english: But from [the fact] that the latter clause is [where] he says "monetary value," the first clause is [where] he does not say "monetary value," as it teaches in the latter clause, etc. - And the same applies that [the Gemara] could have objected directly from the latter clause [of the baraita] against our Mishnah, according to what R' Ḥiyya bar Rav explained: for it teaches in the latter clause, "[If he said: 'The] monetary value of this [bull] is upon me [as] a burnt offering,' the bull is non-sacred and one is not liable for misuse of consecrated property with it; if it dies or is stolen, he does not bear responsibility for it," whereas in our Mishnah we learned that he is obligated to pay! Rather, according to how [the Gemara] began to object from the first clause, it concluded its objection upon it. And according to the answer [in the Gemara], everything is resolved. [However,] there is a difficulty regarding that which is [stated] in the last chapter of Ḥullin (139a and thereabouts): [Regarding] one who consecrates a maneh for the upkeep of the Temple and it was stolen or lost — Rabbi Yoḥanan says: He bears responsibility for it until it comes into the hand of the Temple treasurer. And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: Wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One, as it is written: "The earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof" (Psalms 24:1). [The Gemara there asks:] And [for] items consecrated for the upkeep of the Temple, even though he said "upon me," is he not obligated [to pay]? But we learned [in our Mishnah]: "One who says: 'This bull is a burnt offering,' [or] 'This house is an offering' — if the bull died or the house collapsed, he is exempt from paying; 'This bull is upon me [as] a burnt offering,' [or] 'This house is upon me [as] an offering' — if the bull died or the house collapsed, he is obligated to pay"! Now what is [the Gemara there] objecting?! That [statement] of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish deals with [a case] where he set aside the maneh that he consecrated, and therefore he says that wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One and he is not obligated to pay; whereas that [case] of our Mishnah is where he did not set aside anything [as consecrated], and therefore it teaches that he is obligated to pay — for we established [here] that the bull itself is non-sacred! And it seems that that sugya there does not hold of this [explanation] of R' Ḥiyya bar Rav, who establishes our Mishnah as [referring to] monetary value. Therefore, it seems to Ri that here in our Mishnah, the body of the bull itself is consecrated, like one who consecrates a male [animal] for its monetary value, which is consecrated with intrinsic sanctity (kedushat haguf). And it is not comparable to one who says "his fellow's bull is upon him," where its body is not consecrated — for there a person cannot consecrate his fellow's property, and yet whatever [sanctity] he can make take hold in it, he makes take hold [i.e., a monetary obligation]; but here, where the bull is his own, when he says "[The] monetary value of this bull is upon me [as] a burnt offering," the body of the bull itself is consecrated. And now it is well [understood] why [the Gemara] objects in the last chapter of Ḥullin (ibid.) from this Mishnah against Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: for since the body of the bull itself is consecrated, it is as if he set it aside, and it is comparable to one who consecrates a maneh for the upkeep of the Temple. And it is also well [understood] in our sugya, where [the Gemara] objects from the baraita of "This bull is upon me [as] a burnt offering, etc.," and answers that he said [monetary value], and [nevertheless] the bull is consecrated as it teaches, and so too [in] our Mishnah, the body of the bull itself is consecrated. However, it is somewhat puzzling: why does [the Gemara] need to establish [it], as it concludes [regarding] the first clause [of the baraita], as [a case] where he said "Let the bull be consecrated for its monetary value"? Even without that, since he said "[The] monetary value of this bull is upon me [as] a burnt offering," the body of the bull itself is consecrated! And one must say that this is its explanation: in the first clause, [it is] where he said "Let the bull be consecrated for its monetary value," and the bull becomes consecrated. And one can further say that this [statement] of R' Ḥiyya bar Rav, "They taught [this] only where he said, '[The] monetary value of this bull is upon me [as] a burnt offering,'" means: where he said "Let the bull be consecrated for its monetary value and its monetary value is a burnt offering," and thus the body of the bull is consecrated. And with this, the entire sugya here is resolved, and that [passage] in the final [lit. second] chapter of Ḥullin (ibid.) is also resolved, and [that is why] it objects from our Mishnah here against Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: for since the body of the bull is consecrated, it is as if he set [it] aside, and it is comparable to one who consecrates a maneh for the upkeep of the Temple:
